findings.message: This host did not provide a verified exact author model for the planning review.

The Execution Plan converts the accepted Implementation Plan into one startable, dependency-free slice with an explicit one_pull_request decision and a cohesion-based rationale (observer, authenticated store and verifier form one claim; no unmerged successor). Step 1 begins with the highest-risk named RED, naming its fixture, Node test name, exact command, expected missing-behavior failure and wrong-reason repairs, before any production edit; step 2 requires an approving executable-RED receipt before GREEN. Steps 3-9 keep behavior, matrices, scenario binding, docs/distributions, ordinary verification and the non-substitutable actual-checkout pilot in a readable order. The Proof specifications table precedes the Delivery Checklist; every contributor Required proof resolves to a unique real_boundary proof (observer-real-repository, observer-boundaries, observer-distributions, observer-acceptance, observer-docs), while the partial_or_structural rows (observer-unit, cli-contract, generated-surfaces) discharge nothing. All eleven checklist categories are present with unique IDs, honest contributor ownership, and uniformly open/missing dispositions matching the plan's statement that all implementation is target work and the earlier 257-pass characterization earns no completion. All four Recorded Decisions are accounted for as unchanged; measurement is a recorded skip consistent with the Implementation Plan, and the migration/backfill and scheduled-erasure skips match the accepted data decisions. The checklist obligations cover the accepted 12 blocks / 17 cases (step 5 and the testing item) and preserve the accepted approach - shipped profile, clean committed candidate, isolated clone, fixed runner, authenticated external store, read-only current verification, execution-only authority and unchanged historical evidence. No competing approach, expanded scope, unreviewed design choice or unsupported completion claim appears. No errors remain.

Step 4's acceptance/matrix table gives arrangements and required results per row but defers the concrete command to 'rerun that targeted proof' and the Proof specifications table. That is sufficient because every row runs under observer-boundaries or observer-unit, but a row-level command column would remove the last ambiguity about which parent executes each control.

observer-docs is a review_receipt classified real_boundary. That is defensible because the documentation obligation is maintainer comprehension of purpose, retention, recovery and absent completion authority, which no command can exercise; it does make that one checklist item depend on reviewer judgment rather than an executable boundary.

The slice prerequisites field states 'none' and then lists accepted inputs (12 blocks / 17 cases, approved Implementation Plan, the subordinate 37-case map, pinned tools). These are inputs rather than earlier slices, so dependency ordering remains acyclic and the single merge leaves the repository in a supported state.

execution_plan_record.rationale: The fixed observer, authenticated retained evidence and current-input verifier express one useful claim; shipping any part without the others leaves unusable evidence. The contribution needs no unmerged successor or closing adapter, and the single slice can be understood and proven independently. The rationale rests on conceptual cohesion and independent proof, not line or file count.

slices.boundary: Two proof CLI leaves, fixed T3E4NS profile, isolated runner, private immutable evidence, verifier, acceptance/verification and generated distributions/docs. Excludes certification/closing, shared review or closing gates, historical rewrites, stale #5857 integration, paid qualification, live providers, host enrollment, cloud/OpenCode recovery and shared cache/runtime replacement.
slices.proof: observer-boundaries (real observe/verify CLI, Git, fixed runner, store, retry, freshness, refusals and history under a Node parent), observer-acceptance (all 17 accepted cases through real Cucumber bindings), observer-distributions (npm/unpacked and generated Claude/Codex entrypoints, profiles, recovery, withdrawal), observer-docs (maintainer documentation review receipt) and observer-real-repository (actual committed checkout, unmodified eleven-file lane, 37-case reconciliation, authenticated observation, current verification, unchanged history), with observer-unit, cli-contract, generated-surfaces and ordinary-regression as supporting checks.
slices.completion_signal: All accepted behavior and named matrices pass, the standalone actual-checkout observation and its verification succeed with exit 0, generated entrypoints agree, and all protected original bytes and the 33 deferred identities/owners remain unchanged and uncredited.
